briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Crosses $17B as Federal Psychedelics Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's legal market just topped $17 billion in cumulative sales even as the 24% wholesale tax fight moves onto the gubernatorial trail, with MiCIA now backing a repeal-minded candidate. Nationally, Compass Pathways is racing toward the first-ever psilocybin approval and a federal court just kept marijuana's Schedule III rescheduling intact.

local.text: Michigan cannabis sales cross $17 billion — The CRA's newest monthly report shows combined adult-use and medical sales have reached roughly $17.04 billion since legalization, with August alone bringing in about $259 million.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary plots fall opening — The project is pushing Michigan retail into new territory with a dispensary-and-restaurant format, targeting a fall launch with a full-service restaurant to follow.

Jars Cannabis beats back surveillance overreach — The retailer won removal of a Flock license-plate camera stationed near its Madison Heights store, a rare operator win against local enforcement creep.

Cannabis trade group bets on tax-repeal candidate — MiCIA officially endorsed GOP governor candidate John James, whose commitment to repealing the 24% wholesale tax made him the industry's "clear choice."
Wholesale tax squeeze fuels a repeal campaign — Continued fallout including Zaza Recreational's permanent license surrender is adding momentum to the HB 6224 push to roll back the 24% wholesale tax.

national.text: Compass Pathways nears first psilocybin approval — FDA granted COMP360 a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher and rolling NDA review off Phase 3 depression data, with a submission targeted for Q4 2026.
Federal court keeps marijuana rescheduling on track — The D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge to the medical marijuana Schedule III move on Sept. 9, leaving the reclassification order in effect.

Green Thumb Industries doubles down with buyback — The multistate operator authorized up to $50 million in additional share repurchases running through September 2027, signaling balance-sheet confidence.

Florida clears 22 new medical cannabis licenses — Regulators granted the MMTC licenses after years of litigation stalled the process, opening fresh expansion room in one of the nation's largest medical markets.

FDA pushes ahead on psychedelics despite DEA friction — Even as DEA moves to schedule five psychedelics as Schedule I, FDA is accelerating therapeutic access, though a new GAO report flags gaps in the scheduling process.
